tasks.short: Give public information about parking rules, facilities and local places

steps.what: Clarify the public's parking or location question
Look up current parking regulations, facilities and street or building locations
Explain the parking regulation or directions to the member of public

tasks.design: Index current parking guidance in {DOCS} and bookmark relevant layers in the {OTHER} local mapping application. The worker clarifies the question, checks the actual rule or place and explains it personally; no model or public chatbot is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Moving between guidance and local maps slows straightforward questions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native indexes, bookmarks and links can shorten lookup.
tasks.still_hard: Temporary restrictions and ambiguous location descriptions require checking.
tasks.human_edge: The worker understands what the person needs and explains exceptions clearly.
tasks.altitude: Quicker lookup leaves more time for a clear explanation; enforcement authority is unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native document indexes and map bookmarks can shorten parking-rule and location lookup without automating the public conversation; savings are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes clarifying, looking up and explaining information. Ordinary directions do not require an invented public-contact record; if local procedure requires one, its actual writing must be measured separately.

The municipality's existing rule publisher and map maintainer produce rule text, effective date, area and place location. The worker reads those sources in s2 and clarifies the person's location in s1; there is no free structured address extracted from speech.
Missing, conflicting or stale source information returns to manual checking. No live space-availability flag is assumed.
Test native document search, index pages and map bookmarks first. Full conversation time remains; only actual source navigation loses time.
research_questions: Can the native index reduce lookup without hiding effective dates and temporary exceptions?

already_counted.description: Source checking remains in the lookup step.

incremental.description: Check guidance links and bookmarks for stale restrictions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R89.5, gross10.5 minus2 upkeep gives net8.5. Range2-6 assumes repeated source navigation is currently slow; clarification and explanation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange vehicle towing and direct drivers to the correct vehicle

steps.what: Inspect the illegally parked or abandoned vehicle and its location
Check towing requirements and determine whether removal is authorised
Write the vehicle-removal request and identifying evidence
Send the final towing request to the contracted recovery operator
Direct the tow-truck driver to the exact vehicle and confirm identity
outputs: identified vehicle handed to recovery driver

tasks.design: Configure a short contextual removal-request form in the {OTHER} parking-enforcement application. The worker checks authority, captures actual vehicle evidence, sends the final request and separately identifies the vehicle to the recovery driver.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing a request repeats case context and standard request structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can keep case context while requiring fresh vehicle and location details.
tasks.still_hard: Removal authority and exact vehicle identity require situational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The worker checks the physical vehicle and prevents a mistaken removal.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated request structure; towing authority and on-site verification remain unchanged.

reach.task: Confirm authority and exact vehicle identity before recovery

evidence.claim: Native contextual forms can reduce repeated towing-request fields without replacing removal decisions or actual vehicle checks; the estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes observation, authority check, written removal request, actual external request and on-site vehicle handoff. The worker acts only within existing delegated authority; no new approval is invented.

The worker produces plate, vehicle description, observed location, time, photo reference and removal reason in s1 through s3, with capture time retained. A structured address or valid towing flag is not assumed from an observation.
Missing identity, unclear authority or location uncertainty stops the request for manual resolution. The recovery driver performs the unchanged tow; no supplier saving is claimed.

Test native case-context forms first. Savings concern repeated headings and case identifiers, not actual evidence capture or internal save. Each external handoff checks the version and physical state it actually uses.
unknowns: Local authority and recovery contract procedure
research_questions: Does native form context reduce repeated entry while preserving all fresh vehicle evidence?

already_counted.description: Request capture, final send checks and physical vehicle identification remain counted.

approvals.approved_version: Exact removal request, vehicle identity, location, authority basis and recovery recipient checked before s4 send; changes void the check.
Actual vehicle identity, current location and matching sent request rechecked before s5 recovery handoff; changed circumstances stop the handoff.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R96, gross4 minus1 upkeep gives net3. Range0-1 assumes repeated request structure is currently manual; authority checks, sends and physical handoff retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe and report street hazards and damaged traffic infrastructure

steps.what: Observe hazardous conditions affecting traffic signs, signals and street markings
Capture the hazard location, photographs and factual observations
Write the hazardous-condition report from the captured evidence
Send the final hazardous-condition report to municipal maintenance

tasks.design: Use a native hazard-report form in the {OTHER} municipal field application to replace repeated report structure and attachment arrangement. The worker observes, captures facts and writes the current report, then separately checks and sends it to internal maintenance.
tasks.previous_blocker: An email report repeats location context and attachment arrangement after evidence capture.
tasks.enabler_now: A contextual native form can keep the evidence beside the report fields.
tasks.still_hard: Hazard severity and the exact location require human observation.
tasks.human_edge: The worker recognizes dangerous street conditions and describes what was actually seen.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive report assembly; hazard judgement remains human.

reach.task: Communicate a hazardous road condition precisely

evidence.claim: Native contextual reporting forms can shorten repeated report structure and attachment handling; no automatic hazard detection or measured time saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary includes hazard observation, actual evidence capture, report writing and the final internal send. Immediate urgent communication, if needed, remains manual and is not delayed by the form.

The worker produces location description, observation time, asset description, factual condition and photo reference in s2 at full time. No pre-existing structured hazard code, severity flag or precise address is assumed.
The worker writes the factual report in s3. The form retains evidence context and standard headings only; unclear location or missing evidence returns to manual clarification and ordinary reporting.
Test native municipal forms before code. No automatic routing, alert or external send is implied. Internal draft saves earn no saving; the actual report send has its own final-version check.
unknowns: Whether a native hazard form already exists
research_questions: Does contextual report assembly reduce work after all location and photographic capture remains?

already_counted.description: Evidence capture, actual report writing and final send checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain report fields and maintenance contacts.

approvals.approved_version: Exact hazard report, location, evidence attachments and internal maintenance recipient checked before s4 send; any change voids the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R92.5, gross7.5 minus2 upkeep gives net5.5. Range1-3 assumes real repeated report assembly; observation, capture and final communication retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain the patrol vehicle and report mechanical problems

steps.what: Check vehicle oil, fuel and visible mechanical condition
Perform the permitted simple vehicle maintenance procedures
Write the mechanical-problem report and maintenance observations
Send the mechanical-problem report to the supervisor

tasks.design: Configure a contextual vehicle-problem form in the {OTHER} fleet-maintenance application. Physical checks and simple maintenance stay unchanged; the worker writes actual findings and separately sends the checked report to the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Problem reports repeat vehicle identifiers and standard report structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native vehicle-context forms can remove those repeated fields.
tasks.still_hard: Mechanical symptoms require physical checking and safe judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The worker recognizes a concern that makes continued vehicle use unsafe.
tasks.altitude: A shorter reporting fragment; physical maintenance and vehicle-use judgement stay human.

reach.learn: Clear symptom descriptions and supervisor handoffs

evidence.claim: Native vehicle-context forms can reduce repeated identifiers and report structure without reducing physical checks or maintenance; the estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual vehicle checks, simple maintenance, written problem report and internal supervisor send. No physical step or safety decision is automated.

The worker observes symptoms in s1 and s2 and captures vehicle id, observation time, oil or fuel observation, symptom and maintenance action in s3. The form supplies stable vehicle context only; no structured defect or safe-to-drive flag is assumed.
Missing vehicle identity or unclear symptom description returns to manual reporting and clarification. The supervisor's unchanged decision work receives no saving.
Test native fleet forms before custom code. Savings concern repeated identifiers and report structure, not internal saving or an invented approval. The final send retains its own check.
unknowns: Actual time spent on written mechanical reports
research_questions: Does a contextual form shorten reports after actual symptom capture remains counted?

already_counted.description: Actual report capture and final supervisor-send checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain vehicle-context fields and supervisor contacts.

approvals.approved_version: Exact vehicle-problem report, vehicle id, findings and supervisor recipient checked before s4 send; changes invalidate the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R95, gross5 minus1 upkeep gives net4. Range0-2 assumes avoidable repeated report fields; physical checks, maintenance and actual send retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Patrol observation, public communication and vehicle decisions remain human; selected lookup and written-report fragments become shorter.
reach: Coordinate vehicle and hazard evidence with patrol officers
Share clear defect reporting with security guards
skills_to_grow: Check final versions and recipients before operational handoffs
role.ambitious_version: A worker with clearer field reports and less repeated form work, retaining all enforcement and safety judgement.
